summary: Most probable root cause: the msg-delivery deploy at 08:49 (msg-delivery-00277, batch size increase for delivery receipts) is followed by memory growth from 08:50, a ceiling at 99% by 09:04, OOM kills of workers from 09:05:39, and consumer restarts. Consumers on outbound-msgs dropped to 2, consume rate fell below publish rate, and the queue backed up, which delays and loses replies. The inbound side, the broker and the orchestrator-side dependencies show no sign of being the cause, though several of those checks are summaries only. The link between the deploy and the memory growth is based on timing, not on a code-level confirmation. One early delayed-receipt warning at 08:34 predates the memory rise and is not explained.

hypotheses.statement: The msg-delivery deploy at 08:49 (batch size increase for delivery receipts) causes memory growth from 08:50 to the ceiling by 09:04, after which workers are OOM-killed and restart, consumers drop, and outbound-msgs backs up, delaying or losing replies.
hypotheses.label: high

supporting.text: A msg-delivery deploy with a batch size increase for delivery receipts went out at 08:49, about a minute before memory began to rise. It was the only msg-delivery change recorded in the window.
msg-delivery memory rose off its baseline from 08:50 at about 3 points per minute, with memory warnings starting at 08:50:15 and reaching 99% by 09:04.
The first ERROR in the window across all services is a msg-delivery out-of-memory worker kill at 09:05:39, repeating about every minute. Restarts reached 5 and the error rate climbed to about 0.2.
RabbitMQ shows the first consumer cancellation caused by msg-delivery at 09:05:06, followed by redeliveries of outbound-msgs messages from 09:05:59 in batches of about 7 to 11.

The outbound-msgs queue then backed up: the first depth warning came at 09:09:04 and depth kept rising. Depth peaked at about 2364, consume rate averaged below publish rate and consumers fell to 2. This matches delayed and lost replies, since msg-delivery consumes outbound-msgs and is the last hop before the user.

The rest of the pipeline looks healthy: inbound-msgs has zero depth and constant consumers, and the broker has no errors and low latency. The fault therefore sits at the msg-delivery consumer, not upstream or in the broker.
It is likely that the redeliveries come from messages being re-queued each time a worker is killed. This is a restart-linked retry pattern, not a confirmed retry storm.

contradicting.text: A delayed delivery receipt warning at 08:34:37 on msg-delivery predates the memory rise by about 15 minutes and is not explained by the deploy. It is a single truncated log line and may be background noise.

msg-delivery latency and rps look close to normal, so there is no sign of a latency rise before the memory failure. This neither confirms nor rules out the hypothesis, but it gives no earlier warning signal.

If the 99.0 plateau is a capped reading, true memory use may be higher than shown. Likewise, the claim that this memory climb is the earliest deviation in the pipeline has not been checked against other services' onset times.

hypotheses.statement: A slowdown in llm-gateway (the heaviest orchestrator dependency) delays orchestrator reply production and the outbound-msgs flow, producing late replies independently of msg-delivery.
hypotheses.label: low

contradicting.text: The llm-gateway latency summary shows a narrow range (max about 1517 ms) with no spike. Orchestrator latency also looks flat (max about 966 ms). However, these are window summaries without timestamps, so onset is not ruled out.
inbound-msgs is healthy with zero depth, so orchestrator is consuming normally. The first ERROR in the window came from msg-delivery, not from llm-gateway or orchestrator.
llm-gateway slow-path warnings appear at a sporadic background rate before the onset, which weakens them as the primary cause.
The idea that an llm-gateway slowdown would show up first as orchestrator latency and then as delayed outbound-msgs is an assumption and was not verified.
If llm-gateway were the cause independently, it could coexist with H1. Nothing in the evidence shows it did.

hypotheses.statement: A redis-cache disruption (eviction or restart) causes a cache stampede on portfolio-svc and orchestrator, slowing replies, as in INC-0412.
hypotheses.label: low

contradicting.text: redis-cache slowlog warnings appear at a sporadic background rate before the onset, with no sign of a distinct disruption. No restart or eviction evidence was found.
No config, scaling or other change was recorded for redis-cache or any other service in the window, so there is no trigger like the one in INC-0412. The only changes are the two deploys.
The healthy inbound queue indicates orchestrator is keeping up, which argues against a stampede slowing the reply path.
INC-0412 (Redis restart causing a stampede on portfolio-svc) is a past analogue used only as a hypothesis. It does not show that a Redis restart happened now.

facts.text: msg-delivery memory_pct starts rising off a ~54-57% baseline at 08:50, reaching 58.8% and climbing about 3 points per minute.
The first msg-delivery ERROR in the queried window (from 08:30) is an out-of-memory consumer kill at 09:05:39, and the same error repeats roughly every minute after that.
msg-delivery err_rate summary shows a range up to 0.205 and a last value of 0.203, against a minimum of 0.003, so the error rate went high at some point in the window.
msg-delivery restarts_5m reached 5 and is at 5 at the end of the window.

Other services show only window summaries with no onset information: wa-webhook rps mean 59.877, orchestrator latency_ms mean 902.359 (max 966.078), llm-gateway latency_ms mean 1396.303 (max 1516.663).
msg-delivery latency_ms and rps summaries look close to normal, which weakens the idea that msg-delivery latency rose before the memory failure.
msg-delivery reports memory pressure first at 59% of limit in the WARN stream, the earliest memory warning in the window, and climbs to 99% by 09:04
The earliest msg-delivery anomaly in the WARN stream is a delayed delivery receipt, about 15 minutes before the memory warnings start
The first consumer cancellation on the broker, caused by msg-delivery, occurs at 09:05:06
The first OOM kill of a msg-delivery worker is the first ERROR in the window across all services. The ERROR query returned 83 lines, none truncated, all from msg-delivery
Redelivery of outbound-msgs messages begins at 09:05:59 and recurs in batches of about 7 to 11 messages per restart cycle
The first queue-depth warning for outbound-msgs in the WARN stream is at 09:09:04, with 2 consumers, and depth keeps rising to 598 by 09:18:11
outbound-msgs depth peaked at 2363.688 over the window, with mean 731.796
outbound-msgs consume rate averaged below publish rate (mean 40.988 vs 64.36), and consume rate's last value fell to 25.372
outbound-msgs consumers dropped to 2 (last value), down from a max of 4
outbound-msgs redeliveries reached 10.591 at peak; dead-letter count stayed at 0
inbound-msgs looks healthy: depth 0 throughout, 4 consumers constant, consume rate above publish rate
The RabbitMQ broker itself shows no errors and low latency, so the broker is not the bottleneck
Redis, postgres and llm-gateway slow-path warnings appear before the 09:00 onset at a sporadic background rate, which weakens them as the primary cause
A msg-delivery deploy went out at 08:49 UTC with a batch size change for delivery receipts. It is about 11 minutes before the reported 09:00 onset and is a candidate, not a confirmed cause.
The change query returned only these two items with no truncation, so no config, migration, flag, secret or scaling change was recorded in the window for any listed service.
msg-delivery consumes from the outbound-msgs queue. A change on msg-delivery can therefore affect delivery of messages that orchestrator publishes.
msg-delivery consumes outbound-msgs and is the last hop before delivery.

Past incident INC-0412 (late balance notifications) was attributed to a Redis restart that evicted hot context, causing a cache stampede on portfolio-svc. This is a past incident, used only as a hypothesis.
INC-0412's fix was to restart redis and pre-warm hot keys. This is historical and does not confirm a Redis restart happened in the current incident.

assumptions.text: The flat 99.0 plateau looks like a capped or clamped reading, so the true memory use after 09:04 may be higher than shown.

The memory climb from 08:50 is the earliest deviation in the pipeline, which would make msg-delivery memory exhaustion the root trigger of late or missing replies. This is not yet confirmed against the other services' onset times.
The redelivery counts are consistent with messages being re-queued each time a msg-delivery worker is killed. That is a retry pattern tied to restarts, not a confirmed unbounded retry storm.

Because orchestrator calls llm-gateway with the highest weight and sits between the two queues, a slowdown or failure in llm-gateway would most likely appear first as orchestrator latency and then as delayed outbound-msgs, which would match late or missing replies. This has not been verified.

actions.text: Roll back msg-delivery to the release before msg-delivery-00277, or revert the delivery-receipt batch size increase, then watch memory, restarts and outbound-msgs consumer count return to baseline.
actions.rationale: The deploy 11 minutes before onset is the only msg-delivery change. Memory growth followed it, and the OOM restart loop is what is shrinking outbound consumption.

actions.text: After rollback or restart, confirm that outbound-msgs depth drains and consumers recover to 4. Scale msg-delivery consumers temporarily if the drain is slow. Watch for redelivered duplicates.
actions.rationale: Depth reached about 2364 with consumers at 2 and consume rate below publish rate. Redeliveries are happening with each worker kill, so users may see duplicates, and the dead-letter count of 0 suggests messages were not dead-lettered.

actions.text: Reproduce the batch size change under load in staging and profile memory. Set a safe batch size and a memory limit, and add a canary or memory-growth gate to msg-delivery deploys.
actions.rationale: Memory rose about 3 points per minute from the first minute after the deploy and reached the ceiling in about 14 minutes. A pre-production check would have caught this.

actions.text: Add alerts on msg-delivery memory above a threshold, worker OOM restarts, and outbound-msgs depth and consumer count.
actions.rationale: Memory warnings began at 08:50, but the first queue-depth warning came only at 09:09, and the first ERROR at 09:05, so earlier signals were available.

actions.text: Check the 08:34 delayed delivery receipt warning against the baseline rate to confirm it is background noise rather than a separate issue.
actions.rationale: It predates the deploy and the memory rise and is not explained by the leading cause.
